proposals.title: Add a field without inventing the past
proposals.description: A small table gains one new field while every earlier record keeps its identity and its uncollected value. A later record supplies a value under the expanded schema, leaving the older gaps visible.
proposals.creativeDirection: On a 960x600 React/SVG canvas, frames 0-11 reveal a compact table of earlier records. Frames 12-48 slide the existing columns left and unfold one new column from the header seam. Frames 49-92 place an explicit not-collected mark in that column for each earlier record without changing any original value. Frames 93-132 seat one later record in the same table, with its authored new-field value or missing mark. Frames 133-167 hold both generations under the new header and optional version captions. Frames 168-179 fade to the shared opaque palette ground, giving a deterministic six-second loop at 30fps.
goodFor: Explain an evolving collection form during a changing field program
Show why adding a question does not supply historical answers
Introduce a schema extension before discussing any backfill process
proposals.intent: Separate the addition of a field from the collection of a value for that field.

inputs.name: earlierRecords
inputs.description: Earlier rows whose recorded values remain unchanged throughout the extension.
inputs.constraints: 1..3 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters; labels 1..22 characters; recordedValue 1..18 characters; these rows have no supplied value for the new field

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: The retained column, newly introduced column, and explicit meaning of earlier empty cells.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; labels 1..20 characters; missingLabel must mean not collected, never zero, false, or a negative finding

inputs.name: laterRecord
inputs.description: One later row created under the expanded schema. Null retains a missing mark rather than manufacturing an answer.
inputs.constraints: id 1..16 characters and absent from earlierRecords; label 1..22 characters; recordedValue 1..18 characters; addedValue null or 1..18 characters

inputs.name: phaseLabels
inputs.description: Labels the collection change and the later record without assigning real dates.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; each label 1..30 characters

inputs.name: showVersionLabels
inputs.description: Keeps the before and expanded captions beside the corresponding header outlines.
inputs.constraints: boolean; hiding captions cannot remove missing-value marks or the later-record distinction

inputs.name: evidenceLabel
inputs.description: Keeps the illustrative status and missing-data boundary visible.
inputs.constraints: 1..64 characters; fictional defaults retain an explicit fictional qualifier

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional outreach form initially records a site. It later adds visit mode. Two earlier records retain not-collected visit modes, while a new East record supplies In person.

proposals.distinction: Unlike cell-normalization, this changes the available field structure without correcting existing values. Unlike schema-mapping, no fields are paired across two schemas. Unlike state-preserving-source-refresh, the visible change is a new collection question and its historical absence, not refreshing values from an existing source.
limits: One retained field, one added field, one later row, and at most three earlier rows fit the six-second explanation.
The ending record count is earlierRecords.length + 1. A new column does not create or remove earlier records.
The earlier records always retain missing marks in the added column. No default, imputation, migration, enrichment, or retrospectively inferred answer is shown.
The sequence is a conceptual collection example. It makes no claim about a particular database migration system or any shipped form-editing feature.
The editorial fade resets the illustration, not the stored records. All labels are supplied inputs.
proposals.verificationFocus: Each earlier record retains its ID and existing value, its added-field value stays not collected, and exactly one supplied later record enters. A null later value remains visibly missing.

sourceRefs.rationale: The history identifies rapidly changing collection schemas as a practical crisis-data problem.

sourceRefs.locator: page 5, Key Differentiators and Product Vision
sourceRefs.rationale: The strategy calls for configuration across changing domain needs; the proposal isolates one bounded schema extension.

proposals.title: Fit one new tool to existing data
proposals.description: An optional utility seats into a workspace only after an authored installation choice. Its category-count stencil then reads the retained records and reveals one derived tally, making added capability distinct from data replacement.
proposals.creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal a work surface, a bounded record strip, and an empty tool socket on the 960x600 canvas. Frames 12-55 bring the named utility beside the socket and display the supplied decision. For install, frames 56-90 seat the utility and align its counting stencil with the unchanged category field. Frames 91-132 draw one tally mark per retained record into its category, resolving compact bars on a common integer scale. For defer, the utility stays beside the empty socket and no tally appears. Hold the retained records, decision, and resulting capability through frame 167, then use the shared opaque exit through frame 179. All movement is frame-driven React/SVG at 30fps.
goodFor: Explain an optional extension adding one task-specific capability
Show a team choosing a reusable utility without replacing its dataset
Introduce a plugin concept before a verified installation demonstration
proposals.intent: Show that a chosen extension adds an operation over retained data.

inputs.name: records
inputs.description: Small fictional records counted by the illustrated utility after installation.
inputs.constraints: 1..8 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters; categoryId must reference categories; each record contributes exactly one count

inputs.name: categories
inputs.description: Category labels and display order, including a category with no records if supplied.
inputs.constraints: 2..3 items; unique IDs 1..16 characters; labels 1..18 characters; zero-count categories remain labeled

inputs.name: utility
inputs.description: Names the optional utility and its fixed count-by-category operation.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; labels 1..26 characters; operationLabel must describe counting supplied records by category, not an arbitrary executable operation

inputs.name: installation
inputs.description: Authored human decision controlling whether the capability becomes available.
inputs.constraints: choice install or defer; decisionLabel 1..32 characters and consistent with choice; no automatic install

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: Every workspace, status, result, and example caption.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; each string 1..36 characters; result must describe record counts

inputs.name: showRecordIds
inputs.description: Shows record IDs on the retained strip while each record becomes a tally mark.
inputs.constraints: boolean; each underlying record and category membership remains unchanged

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional lending team chooses to install a category-count utility. The same four source records produce three Books counts and one Tools count. Deferring installation leaves the source records available and the tool slot empty.

proposals.distinction: Unlike dashboard-slot-assembly, a new operation becomes available before it acts on retained data. Unlike pipeline-step-splice, no processing chain is rewired. The socketed stencil visibly derives a result from the existing records rather than introducing a renamed card collection.
limits: One optional utility and one fixed tally operation. No executable code, external URLs, marketplace requests, dependency resolution, or security review occur.
The sum of category counts must equal records.length and each record is counted exactly once. Installation never adds, removes, or edits source records.
The default is fictional. This is not evidence of a shipped plugin system, one-click installation, compatibility with arbitrary data, or a particular installation time.
The defer outcome produces no result and no installed-state marker. Zero-count categories remain visible.
No medical prediction, automated risk assessment, or clinical decision is represented by the utility.
proposals.verificationFocus: The install choice seats exactly one utility and produces category totals from retained record IDs. Defer leaves the socket empty and produces no tally. Changing category membership changes only derived counts.

sourceRefs.rationale: The long-term strategy describes teams installing mission-specific utilities over a common platform; the proposal uses a non-clinical counting example.

proposals.title: Match the reference before comparing a charge
proposals.description: A fictional invoice line is laid over a separate price reference. Only matching procedure, provider, payer, period, and quantity windows permit the amounts to align on one scale; an unmatched context leaves the comparison unresolved.
proposals.creativeDirection: Frames 0-11 reveal a short invoice strip and a separate reference sheet on a 960x600 canvas. Frames 12-70 slide their context windows into vertical registration, retaining a visible notch at each mismatched key. When every key and quantity agrees, frames 71-125 extend the two total-amount rulers from the same zero and open a signed difference bracket. Otherwise the amounts stay separate without a difference bracket. Frames 126-167 hold the matched or unresolved context, source labels, and review caption. Exit to the shared opaque ground at frames 168-179. The six-second React/SVG sequence is deterministic at 30fps.
goodFor: Explain why published prices need the same billing context
Support a fictional price-transparency investigation
Show a discrepancy for review without implying a refund or legal entitlement
proposals.intent: Make the context required for a monetary comparison explicit before showing a difference.

inputs.name: invoice
inputs.description: One fictional billed line with an amount in the shared smallest monetary unit.
inputs.constraints: procedureCode 1..14 characters; providerKey and payerKey 1..22 characters; periodLabel 1..20 characters; quantity integer 1..5; unitPriceMinor integer 0..1000000; no real patient identifiers or real procedure codes in defaults

inputs.name: reference
inputs.description: A separately supplied reference with its own source label.
inputs.constraints: Key bounds match invoice; quantity integer 1..5; unitPriceMinor integer 0..1000000; sourceLabel 1..34 characters; comparison eligibility requires exact equality of all four context keys and quantity

inputs.name: money
inputs.description: Defines one common monetary unit for both lines and the signed difference.
inputs.constraints: currencyLabel 1..18 characters; minorUnitsPerUnit exactly 1 or 100; both lines use this same currency and unit scale; no exchange-rate conversion

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: All visible context, outcome, and evidence labels.
inputs.constraints: All keys required; key labels 1..16 characters; outcome labels 1..32 characters; review and example 1..52 characters

inputs.name: focus
inputs.description: Chooses whether the matched windows or the amount rulers receive the final emphasis.
inputs.constraints: keys or amounts; amount focus never hides unmatched context or creates a comparison

inputs.name: showDifference
inputs.description: Shows the signed total-amount difference only after complete context agreement.
inputs.constraints: boolean; totals are quantity times unitPriceMinor; difference equals invoice total minus reference total; mismatch suppresses both numeric difference and difference geometry

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional billed line for DEMO-P1 at Demo clinic A under Demo plan Q in Demo period A is 84 demo credits for one unit. A separately supplied reference for the same context is 60 demo credits. The illustration exposes a 24-credit difference for review, without deciding what is owed.

proposals.distinction: Unlike benefit-shortfall-correction, no payment is corrected and no unpaid amount is treated as an entitlement. Unlike paired-contrast, exact context keys govern whether a numeric comparison is allowed. Unlike keyed-row-zipper, the records remain separate and open an amount ruler rather than becoming a joined dataset.
limits: This is a fictional one-line comparison. It is not a medical billing interpretation, legal determination, price guarantee, negotiation result, or refund claim.
Totals use exact integer arithmetic in the shared smallest unit. The signed difference may be negative, positive, or zero; no automatic favorable result is implied.
A mismatch in any context key or quantity leaves the comparison unresolved. Similar text is not treated as a match, and no real CPT or payer taxonomy is inferred.
The ruler uses a common zero and a domain derived from the larger supplied total. For two zero totals use a one-minor-unit display domain without changing either value.
Currency, quantities, source label, period, and fictional status stay visible at the resolved hold. Published reference prices can have qualifications outside this bounded example.

Compute the active distribution using integer basis-point arithmetic. Reject fractional minor-unit distributions or negative retained amounts.
Both periods are separate flows over equal durations. Do not carry the first remainder into the second tray or display their sum as a company balance.
